findings.comment: Inspector observed ice machine in back storage area to be soiled with black residue on the exterior baffles. findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed tomatoes and lettuce in the kitchen drawer cooler measure 51F with the probe. PIC was informed, and since the items were recently moved to the drawer cooler to the walk-in, the items were returned to the walk-in cooler. This violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The drawer cooler in the kitchen measured 53F with the infrared and probe thermometers. The digital display on the exterior of the cooler read 43F. The PIC was informed that the cooler was not functioning and the food items inside were moved to the walk-in cooler. This cooler is not adequate for holding time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods until it is repaired. The walk-in cooler will be used until repairs are complete. A follow-up is scheduled for July 7th (accommodating the holiday and weekend) to ensure the cooler has been repaired.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed hand sink in kitchen to be obstructed with paper towels and dish soap in sink basin. Informed PIC of issue, and items were removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sink is easily accessible at all times to promote frequent and proper hand washing. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed molded sliced tomato in prep cooler drawer. PIC was informed of unsafe food, and the tomatoes were discarded. To avoid serving unsafe food to the public, ensure cut produce is clearly date marked and discarded after 7 days. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer spray bottle in the kitchen to “bleach out” test strip, indicating that the solution was too potent. PIC was informed that sanitizer was too strong, and the bottle was diluted. Ensure bleach sanitizer solutions are at an appropriate concentration to avoid toxicity. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed produce in prep cooler (tomato, lettuce, onion) and walk-in cooler (salads, creamer, milk) to have no date mark. Informed PIC that time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods that are considered ready-to-eat need to be date marked and discarded after 7 days. A follow-up has been scheduled for 3/20/2025 to ensure date marking compliance.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed hood in kitchen to be soiled dust and grease. Observed chest freezer in back storage area to be soiled with old food (french fries). Informed PIC that chest freezer and hood are in need of a cleaning. Routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces prevents cross-contamination with food and food-contact surfaces. Ensure that surfaces are clean for next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 
Observed containers of seasoning to be stored on bread crates that are not at least six inches above the floor. Crates are also difficult to clean around and often lead to other issues. Discontinue this practice and provide proper storage for these items.

findings.comment: Observed wet wiping cloth to be stored on the coffin cooler during lunch rush. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

(C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430. Employees shall obtain the handler certification within 30 days of hire.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Chili is 125°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Observed deli meat packages to be thawing at room temperature on the prep table in the kitchen. Time and temperature control for safety (TICS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13. Properly thaw foods for safety. Foods were placed into the cooler for thawing.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee came in from smoke break and was observed washing hands without proper technique. Employee shut off the manual faucet at the bar with bare hands. Proper technique was discussed. Employee rewashed hands using proper technique, and paper towels were used as a barrier to shut off the faucet after process was completed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Use proper technique every time with the final step being to dry hands and then use the paper towels to shut off the manual faucet to avoid potential re-contamination of freshly washed hands.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - A) Clean dishes were observed on a dish rack in the third compartment of the 3 part sink. Per the approved variance request dishes are to be stored with a barrier (metal or plastic rack) in the first or second compartment between lunch and dinner service only to allow bartenders access to the counter space across from the sink. Equipment is to be stored in the designated storage area at the close of operations each night. Also, the automatic paper towel dispenser was not working, and paper towels, located over third compartment, had to be retrieved to dry hands during handwashing process. Policy was discussed for ware washing and clean equipment storage variance.
NOTE: The automatic paper towel dispenser is located above the first compartment of the 3 part sink. The only option for storage of dishes between lunch and dinner according to the approved variance request would now be in the second compartment if paper towels are to be present over the first and third compartments of the sink. Follow the guidelines of the approved policy and store items properly.

B) Pizza slicer was observed in the crevice between the top of the microwave and the bottom of the pizza oven. Cease the practice of storing utensils in crevices between equipment. 

C) Bag of bread was observed in direct contact with clean knives on the counter in the kitchen. The outer surface of the bread bag is not considered clean and should not be stored in direct contact with the food contact surfaces of clean equipment or single service articles. 

Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

findings.citation_text:

Solution was remade using warm water and 4 tablets instead of 2; concentration of new solution was +200ppm. 

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Maintain quat solution at 200-400ppm (per instructions on bottle), and use warm water when making solutions.
**Make sure to follow the instructions when mixing sanitizer solution; instructions state to make solution using warm water. The temperature of the water can affect the concentration**

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Foods stored in the right end of the bar cooler across from the 3 part sink were observed at temperatures above 41F. Products all had labels that said "Refrigerate After Opening". Items included dilled brussel sprouts (52F-53F); bloody mary mix (58F-60F); olives (49F-50F). The aforementioned items were discarded in the trash. Sliced citrus and cherries (label lacking refrigaration requirement) were kept for use. The cooler was holding much colder in the middle and left end of the unit. Cold PHF should not be stored in the unit on the right side until it is holding consistently at proper temperatures, and that includes any mixers that contain fruit juice and require refrigeration after opening. (See general comments)

Cold PHF shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 41FF/below at all times during storage.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.210 - Chili, cheese sauce, and taco meat reheating in counter-top food warmer were not at 165F. Prior to leaving owner stated the reheating process began some time around 8a. Internal temperatures were checked for foods at ~9:55a and were observed at 145F (chili), 160 (cheese sauce), and 77F-85F (taco meat). Cook noted the taco meat was pulled from the freezer the night prior. Based on the information provided the foods were not rapidly reheating to 165F and would not reach proper temperature by 10a. Cook immediately placed all three pans of food on the grill to finish rapidly reheating items to 165F/above.

NOTE: If the food warmer gets hot enough to rapidly/properly reheat PHF, then the unit can be used for reheating and hot holding purposes. However, if it can not reheat foods to 165F/above w/in 2hrs then it can only be used for hot holding purposes to maintain foods at 135F/above after products have been properly reheated using cooking equipment such as the microwave, grill, or stove.

PHF shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout the product. Properly reheat food to 165°F or above.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Beer cooler across from 3 part sink used for storage of PHF did not have a thermometer inside. Provide a thermometer for the cooler, and make sure all coolers and freezers used for storage of PHF have functioning thermometers inside. 

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Boxes of cups were observed on the back stairwell in the storage area at the southwest end of the building. Store single service articles up off the floor at least 6 inches regardless of packaging. 

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Deli meats in the kitchen cooler had a date mark of 5/15, and hotdogs in the same cooler had a date mark that was not legible. Also, soup in the walkin cooler had a date mark of 5/18. The aforementioned foods were discarded in the trash. Proper date marking was discussed.
Ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be clearly dated and consumed, sold, or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
Make sure the date is changed to reflect proper thaw and use by dates when ready to eat, PHF is pulled from the freezer for use.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.210 - Chili and BBQ placed in hot holding unit after being reheated on the stove had internal temperatures at 129F and 131F-145F respectively. All foods were placed back on the stove to get up to 165F. A high temperature thermometer was used when the owner checked the reheat temperatures initially. A digital thermometer that registers hot and cold temperatures was used to ensure proper reheat temperature was reached.  PHF shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout the product. Properly reheat food to 165F/above.
Make sure the hot holding unit is on well in advance to hold foods at 135F/above after foods have been properly reheated to 165F on the stove. When reheating in roasters, make sure soups and other foods are being stirred frequently to help heat foods evenly/quickly.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Ranch dressing in kitchen cooler had an internal temperature of 48F. Owner was unsure as to how long the dressing may have been out of the cooler at lunch time. Cook was not present to answer questions. Ranch was voluntarily discarded by owner.
Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be maintained at 41F/below. Maintain cold PHF at proper temperature.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Inside blue ice scoop holder was soiled. Owner cleaned and sanitized the ice scoop holder during the inspection. 
Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice. **Clean and sanitize the ice scoop holder daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris**

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Italian beef in kitchen cooler was at 102F (surface temp) and 129F (internal temp). Cook stated product was pulled from hot holding well at end of lunch (~2p) and placed directly in cooler. Per request of inspector, Italian beef was placed in an ice bath in the walkin cooler to speed up cooling process. Temperature dropped below 50F during the inspection. Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in additional 4 hrs. The only way to verify foods are cooling properly in the designated time frame is to use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to monitor products during cooling process. Benefit of doubt was given for Italian beef today, and cook was allowed to speed up the cooling process to keep food. However, questionable foods may be discarded at the discretion of inspector. Do not place hot foods directly into the kitchen cooler for the purposes of cooling. The kitchen cooler is not intended to cool hot foods but rather maintain cold foods at 41F/below. Placing hot/warm foods inside the kitchen cooler can compromise the ability of cooler to maintain temperature as well as the safety of foods inside.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Chicken tortilla soup was at 67F-124F inside a small roaster in the walkin cooler. A new bag (cold product) was placed in the removable pan prior to placing the whole unit in the walkin for lunch tomorrow. The bottom heating element was still warm  and caused the soup to get warm. Cook was allowed to keep the product. It was placed in an ice bath to rapidly drop the temperature. Temperature dropped to 48F-61F w/in the half hour and continued cooling to proper temperature. Cook and owner were advised if any soup is leftover after it is served at lunch tomorrow the product needs to be discarded. Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below. **Do not put the inner pan in the roaster if heating element is still warm and cold foods are not ready to be heated**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) Shelves in kitchen cooler were rusty/rough in a few places. Clean and paint the shelves. B) Bottom inside upright freezer had a layer of ice accumulation, and a hole was observed on the bottom left side. De-frost the freezer, and repair the damaged area. C) Three door freezer had heavy ice accumulation throughout. De-frost the 3 door freezer. D) Top inner edge of chicken freezer had damaged spots where insulation was exposed. Repair the damaged areas. Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) glass holding markers on shelf above kitchen door (debris); B) grill - waste tray/area between tray and grill surface (carbon/debris); C) table holding grill (dust/debris); D) counter under microwave and food warmer (crumbs/debris); E) top of microwave below pizza ovens (dust/crumbs); F) inside fryer (dust/debris); & G) stove - top around burners and waste tray/area below burners (debris). Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - Floors were observed to be soiled in the following areas: A) bar - floor to wall juncture throughout (bottle caps/debris); B) under the ice machine (debris); & C) under cooking equipment in kitchen (general debris & an old rodent trap with dust on it). Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas. Floors shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Absence of labeling to cole slaw and chili meat in the beer walking cooler.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Label the food product.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed in the small white chest freezer in the back room to have fully cooked chicken stored with raw chicken. (CORRECTED)
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Absence of chemical test kit to check sanitize in the 3 compartment sink. Owner has Cl test kit. Using sterimine tablets.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. Quat-200ppm-

findings.comment:

750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed utensils in the kitchen in bucket to be stored upright with handle down.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.
